Guidance & outlook: In our tire recycling businesses for Reclaim Rubber, for example, we expect volumes in FY 2027 to grow by close to 20% over the prior year.

In our plastic recycling business, our nylon and polyolefin recycling verticals, we expect over a 20% growth this fiscal, followed by a mid -teen growth through FY 2030, while maintaining a stable EBITDA margin of between 10% to 15%, supported by tightening EPR regulation and our continued focus on value-added products.
This is well ahead of our stated target of 50% by FY 2028, which we should reach in the current fiscal.
Growth & demand: The consolidated total income for the quarter grew 26% year -on-year to INR1,573 million on the back of volume growth, mainly attributable to the Pyrova Energy capacity utilization and improving realizations with both domestic and export markets contributing meaningfully.

On a stand-alone basis, the segment revenue grew 34%, of which Reclaim volumes grew 12% GRP Limited July 27, 2026 and reclaim export volumes rebounded 20%, as customer order patterns normalized following the easing of U.S. tariffs.
Engineering Plastics grew volumes 27%, helped by domestic automotive demand and a more favourable virgin nylon pricing environment.
Margins & costs: Importantly, that growth led to an EBITDA rise of 60% to INR174 million and EBITDA margin expansion by 233 basis points to 11%, even as raw material costs rose sharply during the quarter.

Together, our plastic verticals expanded EBITDA margins by 14 percentage points year -on- year on a 10-point improvement in gross margin, reflecting a better product and customer mix and continued cost discipline.
While gross margin moderated on higher raw material costs, EBITDA margin expanded to 11% from 8.7% on operating leverage and efficient cost management.
Capex & expansion: During the quarter, the plant achieved its longest continuous reactor run since commissioning, an important milestone because stable, continuous operation is the precursor to throughput, reliability, and commercial performance in a continuous pyrolysis process.

On profitability, we expect margins to build from a single digit during the ramp -up stage that we are currently in to move towards 18% to 20% once the rCB facility is commissioned, operational and mature with customer approvals.
Our rCB plant is under commissioning -- will be under commissioning starting next month and hopefully will be commissioned by October of 2026.
Balance sheet & cash: In the quarter of significant input cost inflation, operating leverage, product mix and cost discipline did the heavy lifting.
Beyond the operating performance, we improved our working capital cycle by 8 days to 86 days, reflecting continued operational discipline.
